1.title: Silurian Schist: A Geology Unique in Alsace
1.html:
Kastelberg lies on the north side of Andlau village, a small steep hill facing southeast at 240–300 m, with an area of only 5.82 hectares.

Its geological foundation is Silurian Steige schist — a geological type unique in Alsace — metamorphosed by the neighbouring Andlau granite (located above the site) into an extremely hard, dark-coloured rock composed mainly of quartz, mica and chlorite, producing very well-drained, stony soils.
2.title: An Ancient Vineyard from Roman Times
2.html:
Kastelberg is one of the oldest vineyards in Alsace — vines were already planted here during the Roman occupation. A document of 1064 already records that the site produced "great wines" (grands vins).

As early as 1850, Andlau's growers were already selling wine commercially under the name "Riesling Kastelberg" — more than a century before the 1975 Grand Cru decree gave it official recognition.
3.title: The Riesling Style of Kastelberg
3.html: Kastelberg is authorised for only one variety, Riesling. The schist soil gives the wines a clear varietal character (race) and vigour (virilité), plus delicate, restrained aromas — inheriting everything this unique terroir offers, and making excellent ageing wines.
4.question: What is unique about Kastelberg's geological foundation?
4.options.0: It is the only volcanic site in Alsace
4.options.1: It is the only schist site in Alsace — Silurian Steige schist metamorphosed by neighbouring granite into a hard, dark rock
4.options.2: It is the largest Grand Cru in Alsace
4.options.3: It is the only Grand Cru that allows blending
4.explanation: Kastelberg's geological foundation is Silurian Steige schist, a geological type unique in Alsace, metamorphosed by the neighbouring Andlau granite into a hard, dark rock (quartz, mica, chlorite). It therefore stands alone in Claude Sittler's ten-family classification as the only member of the "schist" family.
